senses.gloss:
Aukṣa-gandhi (‘having the smell of bull's grease’) appears in the Atharvaveda as the name of an Apsaras, beside other names, of which Guggulū and Naladī clearly indicate plants. This name, therefore, presumably also denotes some sort of fragrant plant. aukṣa in the same Saṃhitā means ‘bull's grease’ (from akṣan, ‘bull’).
Foot notes iv. 37. 3.
ii. 36. 7.
Cf. Zimmer, Altindisches Leben, 69; Bloomfield, Hymns of the Atharvaveda, 324; Whitney, Translation of the Atharvaveda, 211, 212, and on aukṣa, ibid., 82, 83.
